items.title: Stryker stock falls on slower peripheral vascular, hip sales
items.summary: Stryker shares fell after the cyberattack on its Microsoft environment (confirmed 04/09) disrupted its peripheral vascular business, acquired last year, and hip sales weakened. Stock down more than 10% in the week following the incident.

items.title: CX co-chair receives VIVA 2026 LIVE Award
items.summary: Charing Cross (CX) Symposium co-chair Andrew Holden (Auckland City Hospital, Auckland, New Zealand) received the VIVA Foundation’s 2026 LIVE Award yesterday morning.

items.title: Endologix rebrands as Rhevera Medical
items.summary: Endologix Holdings has announced Rhevera Medical as its new corporate brand—an updated identity that reflects the company’s broader commitment to partnering with physicians who treat complex vascular disease, and supporting patients whose lives, mobility and independence depend on the company’s technologies, as stated…

items.title: Sirolimus-eluting balloon achieves patency results in line with best-in-class paclitaxel devices, VIVA audience hears
items.summary: The Selution sustained limus release (SLR) Sustane drug-eluting balloon (DEB; MedAlliance/Cordis) has achieved patency results (90.3%) in line with best-in-class paclitaxel devices and the highest reported Kaplan-Meier (KM) rate in a superficial femoral artery (SFA) investigational device exemption (IDE) trial to…

items.title: AMA assigns new CPT codes for renal denervation
items.summary: The American Medical Association (AMA) has approved two new category I current procedural terminology (CPT) codes describing renal denervation.

items.title: First patient enrolled in Gore Excluder IBE Plus stent graft pivotal study
items.summary: Gore announced today the first patient enrolment in the IBE Plus pivotal study, a clinical trial evaluating the investigational Gore Excluder iliac branch endoprosthesis (IBE) Plus stent graft for the treatment of aortoiliac and common iliac artery aneurysms.

items.title: Inquis Medical launches “first” thrombectomy catheter with full 360-degree directional aspiration for PE
items.summary: Inquis Medical has announced the US commercial launch of its latest Aventus catheter, which is designed to provide physicians with 360-degree sweeping directional aspiration for clot removal within the vasculature.

items.title: Medtronic receives US FDA Breakthrough Device designation for IN.PACT BTK drug-coated balloon
items.summary: Medtronic has received US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Breakthrough Device designation for its IN.PACT below-the-knee (BTK) drug-coated balloon.

items.title: “Huge variation in practice”: Early insights from the European Venous Registry
items.summary: The European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) European Venous Registry (EVeR) is set to elucidate clinical practice patterns for the management of deep venous disease, with the aim of improving long-term patient outcomes.

items.title: iPerf concludes clinical trial of novel dual-lumen femoral arterial cannula for cardiopulmonary support
items.summary: iPerf has announced the conclusion of its first clinical trial evaluating its dual-lumen femoral arterial cannula for cardiopulmonary support.

items.title: SWEDEPAD 2 sparks guideline update for asymptomatic PAD and intermittent claudication
items.summary: The European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) has incorporated new evidence, predominantly from SWEDEPAD 2, into updated recommendations on the management of asymptomatic peripheral arterial disease (PAD) and intermittent claudication.

items.title: UK Government backs major vascular care reforms—now it must turn words into action, says Circulation Foundation
items.summary: The Circulation Foundation—the UK’s leading vascular charity—is calling on the UK Government to move swiftly from agreement to action following a landmark Westminster Hall debate on vascular health, in which members of parliament (MPs) united behind the need for urgent reform of vascular services.

items.title: Mölnlycke launches Biogel radiation protection gloves to reduce clinician hand exposure during procedures
items.summary: Mölnlycke Health Care US announced today the launch of a new surgical glove range designed to reduce clinician hand exposure to scattered radiation during fluoroscopy-guided, interventional and other image-dependent procedures.

items.title: BD collaboration brings immersive vascular case observation to Europe
items.summary: This advertorial, sponsored by BD, is only intended for readers in Europe.

items.title: Anahita Dua
items.summary: With interests ranging from precision medicine for peripheral arterial disease (PAD) to surgical outreach and political advocacy, Anahita Dua (Boston, USA) sees the boundaries of vascular surgery extend well beyond the operating room.

items.title: “A different way of innovating”: Cross-disciplinary team tackles endograft removal
items.summary: A team of researchers are combining expertise in vascular surgery and engineering to develop a novel device for endograft explantation.

items.title: Reduced noise, increased visibility: OPTIQ AI leads to “easier and more reliable” procedures
items.summary: Sitting down in the CX Studio at CX 2026, Markus Steinbauer (Krankenhaus Barmherzige Brüder, Regensburg, Germany) shares his thoughts on a new artificial intelligence (AI)-powered imaging chain from Siemens Healthineers: OPTIQ AI.

items.title: Humacyte announces US FDA authorisation extending Symvess shelf life to 36 months
items.summary: Humacyte recently announced that the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorised an extension of the expiration dating period for Symvess (acellular tissue engineered vessel-tyod, or ATEV) from 18 months to 36 months when stored refrigerated at 2–8 degrees Celsius (36–46 degrees Fahrenheit).

items.title: Penumbra launches Link clot capture device for arterial thrombectomy
items.summary: Penumbra recently launched the Link clot capture device, which is intended to support the removal of arterial thrombus when used in conjunction with Lightning Bolt technology.

items.title: Two-year trial results support sirolimus-eluting balloon for patients with failing AVFs
items.summary: Treatment with a sustained-release sirolimus-eluting balloon (SLR) for patients with failing arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) was associated with higher target-lesion primary patency (TLPP) through to two-year follow-up, with a favourable safety profile to high-pressure plain balloon angioplasty alone.

items.title: “It tracks our learning curve as we transitioned from largely open first to almost exclusively endovascular first”
items.summary: Jayer Chung (Baylor College of Medicine, Houston, USA) digs into new data showing similar outcomes between open- and endovascular-first revascularisation treatment strategies for acute limb ischaemia (ALI). Watch the full interview here.

items.title: Acute limb ischaemia study: 90-day outcome metrics “were largely the same, if not better, for endovascular-first approaches”
items.summary: Jayer Chung (Baylor College of Medicine, Houston, USA) speaks to Vascular News about the explosion in percutaneous treatment options for the care of patients with acute limb ischaemia (ALI) in recent years.

items.title: Lessons from two decades of carotid stent use: Implications for today’s practice
items.summary: This advertorial, sponsored by Abbott, is only intended for readers in the USA. Peter Faries (Mount Sinai Health System, New York, USA) recounts his extensive clinical experience in the field of carotid stenting, highlighting design developments, procedural advances, and pivotal data.

items.summary: Vascular News caught up with Fabrizio Fanelli (Careggi University Hospital, Florence, Italy) at the Cardiovascular and Interventional Radiological Society of Europe (CIRSE) annual congress (5–9 September, Copenhagen, Denmark) to discuss the recent European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) guideline update on…

items.title: STRIKE-PE subanalysis finds durable functional and quality-of-life outcomes for CAVT
items.summary: A subanalysis of the STRIKE-PE trial has provided evidence that treatment with the 16Fr Lightning Flash (Penumbra) computer-assisted vacuum thrombectomy (CAVT) device is associated with longer-term benefits, including improvements in functional and quality-of-life outcomes in patients with pulmonary embolism (PE).
